key_insight: Bias in multi-agent LLM aggregation can be controlled to choose better initial answers and deliberately injected to reveal when an agent’s decision is unreliable.
engineering_relevance: The method offers a practical test-time aggregation strategy that improves accuracy and token efficiency without needing validation data or prior model-strength calibration.
method: Present one style-normalized reasoning trace for each distinct answer to reduce non-semantic bias.
Place each aggregating agent’s own initial answer in the minority to induce instability as a reliability signal.
Aggregate results without changing existing debate or Mixture-of-Agents interaction/synthesis pipelines.
evidence_signal: Across three mathematical reasoning benchmarks and four heterogeneous LLM combinations, the framework outperformed non-oracle aggregation methods and also improved final-answer accuracy in multi-agent debate and Mixture-of-Agents.
watch_item: The approach depends on carefully constructed prompts and answer grouping, so performance may be sensitive to how distinct answers are normalized and presented.
paper_title: Bias Control and Injection for Multi-Agent Aggregation
